newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB likely to leave debenture coupon unch -bankers.
newsitem.headline: NCB likely to leave debenture coupon unch -bankers.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) is likely to either leave the coupon for its January five-year debentures unchanged at 2.15 percent or raise it by only 0.1 percentage point despite the sharp rise in its December debenture yield in the secondary market, bankers said on Wednesday.
The bank is likely to leave its long-term prime rate for January unchanged at a record low 2.5 percent, they said.
NCB and Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd are expected to announce their prime rates and the coupon rates of their January debentures on Thursday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), the largest of the three long-term credit banks, announced on Wednesday it would leave its January long-term prime rate unchanged at 2.5 percent.
IBJ also said it will leave the coupon rate on its January five-year debentures unchanged at 1.6 percent.

"There is no change in our stance in respect to the market trend in setting the terms for new debentures, but the recent rise (in NCB debenture yield in the secondary market) is overdone. Hence, we are not going to 100 percent follow the market trend," an official at NCB said.
Bankers said NCB has little room available to raise its debenture coupon as the long-term prime rate stood at 2.5 percent.
NCB's five-year debenture with a 2.15 percent coupon issued in December was traded at a yield of around 3.06 to 3.07 percent in the secondary market on Wednesday, traders said.
Meanwhile, a five-year debenture with a 1.6 percent coupon issued by IBJ was traded at a yield of 1.70 percent.
